name: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport
before:
Telangana's airport, at Shamshabad about 24 km south of Hyderabad, and fourth busiest in India with over 29 million passengers in the year to March 2025. It also handled more than 167,660 tonnes of cargo.

It was India's first greenfield airport built as a public private partnership, and at 2,200 hectares it is the largest in the country by area. Only about a third of that is developed, with the rest held for expansion, and the operator has said no further land will be acquired.

It has a record of going first on technology. It was the first airport in India to launch domestic e-boarding, in December 2015, and added international e-boarding in October 2020. AirHelp has ranked it among the top ten airports in the world.

There are two runways. The primary one is 4,260 metres, ILS equipped and long enough for an A380. The second, inaugurated in February 2012 and converted from a taxiway, takes aircraft up to an A340 or 747 and is used mainly when the main runway is being maintained.

It opened in March 2008, replacing Begumpet, and is named after Rajiv Gandhi.
after:
Telangana's airport, at Shamshabad about 24 km south of Hyderabad, and fourth busiest in India with more than 30 million passengers in the year to March 2026. That year it also handled more than 180,000 tonnes of cargo.

It was built as a greenfield airport under a public private partnership, and was the first airport in India to introduce e-boarding.

There are two runways. At 4,260 metres, the main one is long enough for an A380. The second is the parallel taxiway, which serves as the standby runway.

It opened in March 2008 and is named after Rajiv Gandhi.

claims.note: AAI's state table for April 2025 to March 2026 gives Telangana 30,494,254 passengers; Rajiv Gandhi International carried 30,483,885 of them and the old Begumpet airport the other 10,369.
